Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

amaze verb

also astonish, astound, amazing, be amazed, stunned

classical

Ter. Ph. 2.1.54: eum timidum obstupefēcit pudor (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 2.10 (Lewis & Short)

obstupefaciō, obstupefacere, obstupefēcī, obstupefactum

verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive; passive obstupefīō

amaze, astound

To strike someone dumb with wonder (or with fear or shame).

Other words

  • attonitus, attonita, attonitum — amazed, stunned

    adjective (participle of attonō), declension · also used · classical · Liv. 22.17.5: mīrāculō attonitī

    Literally “thunderstruck”: the usual way to say “amazed” of people who stop dead.

  • stupeō, stupēre, stupuī — be amazed, stand stunned

    verb, second conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Ter. And. 2.1.4 (Lewis & Short); Prud. Cath. 7.130

    To be dazed with astonishment; also, of the body, to be numb.

Examples

  • veluti flammās spīrantium mīrāculō attonitī cōnstitērunt

    they stood still, amazed at the wonder, as if the oxen were breathing fireLiv. 22.17.5

  • ructātus exit sēque servātum stupet

    belched out, he comes forth amazed to be savedPrud. Cath. 7.130

See also be surprised, surprise, wonder.
